sentences.text: In Norway, a vote in the far north counts almost twice as much as a vote in Oslo.
Who can vote? Norwegians who turn 18 in the election year, even abroad.
One ballot paper per party: pick one, fold it, get it stamped, drop it in the box.
Seats go to 19 districts by people and land: Finnmark gets a seat per 14,000 voters, Oslo per 26,000.
Parties above 4% get top-up seats to match the national vote.
That's 169 seats in the Storting, which makes the laws and sets taxes.
A prime minister needs no vote to take office, just no majority against them.
The King appoints the government and signs every law. Since August: Haakon VIII.
In 2025, Labour won 53 seats, Progress 47, and Jonas Gahr Støre stayed on, governing alone.
And Norway's parliament can never be dissolved. No early elections. Stability, or democracy on pause?
